To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have identified optical counterparts to 60 of the unconfirmed Planck cluster candidates; 2) 12 of these candidates have no optical counterpart but are expected to be clusters at z> 0.8; 3) we have measured redshifts for 210 of the 387 Planck cluster candidates, and have estimated redshifts for the remaining 177.
60 out of the 237 Planck candidates have confirmed counterparts, 94 have no counterpart and 83 are too heavily contaminated by stars to attempt confirmation.
60 of the 150 clusters in the Planck Early Sunyaev–Zeldovich (ESZ) cluster sample have optical counterparts and measured redshifts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the Planck galaxy cluster sample.
the study of the galaxy cluster population detected via the SZE in thePlanck all-sky maps and the use of optical data to characterize their physical properties.
the study of the optical counterparts of the Planck galaxy cluster candidate sample, with a particular emphasis on the redshifts of the clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
72 of the 150 Planck galaxy cluster sample have been confirmed, and we have identified an additional 60 new galaxy clusters.

we are able to measure redshifts for all but 3 per cent of the 150 confirmed clusters, we are able to identify counterparts for 25 per cent of the unconfirmed clusters, we are unable to identify a counterpart due to contamination by stars for 35 per cent of the candidates, and we have estimated redshift limits for 40 per cent of the remaining candidates.
60 of the 150 confirmed clusters have been confirmed by our analysis and that the 12 unconfirmed candidates have a 20% probability of being real clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
of the 387 candidates we examined in this study, 60 were confirmed as real clusters, while for 94 candidates no optical counterpart could be found and 233 are heavily contaminated by stars.
we have confirmed the redshifts of 150 Planck clusters and identified 60 additional confirmed clusters.

we have confirmed 60 out of 150 Planck galaxy cluster samples with redshifts, 12 of which are unconfirmed, and have identified 83 candidates that we are unable to confirm due to heavy contamination by Galactic stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Planck SZE selected galaxy cluster candidates can be confirmed and their redshifts measured with a single deep imaging observation.
Pan-STARRS imaging data is a powerful tool for confirming and measuring redshifts for galaxy clusters identified in the Planck SZE catalogue.
the Pan-STARRs imaging data are very well suited to the confirmation of the Planck galaxy clusters.
